claim: Laboratory mice develop populations of circulating memory CD4+ T cells in the absence of overt infection.
source: Laboratory mice develop populations of circulating memory CD4+ T cells in the absence of overt infection.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract that establishes a foundational observation about memory CD4+ T cells in laboratory mice.

claim: Memory CD4+ T cell populations are replenished from naive precursors at high levels throughout life.
source: We have previously shown that these populations are replenished from naive precursors at high levels throughout life (Gossel et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: There is evidence for sequential naive to central memory to effector memory development.
source: We found evidence for sequential naive to central memory to effector memory development
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on the experimental data and modeling.

claim: Both memory subsets (TCM and TEM) are heterogeneous in their rates of turnover.
source: and confirmed that both memory subsets are heterogeneous in their rates of turnover.
evidence: This is a finding confirmed by the current study's data and modeling approaches.

claim: Early exposure to self and environmental antigens establishes persistent memory populations at levels determined largely, although not exclusively, by the dirtiness of the environment.
source: We also inferred that early exposure to self and environmental antigens establishes persistent memory populations at levels determined largely, although not exclusively, by the dirtiness of the environment.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from comparing mice in different housing conditions.

claim: After the first few weeks of life, memory populations are continuously supplemented by new memory cells at rates that are independent of environment.
source: After the first few weeks of life, however, these populations are continuously supplemented by new memory cells at rates that are independent of environment.
evidence: This is a key finding from comparing clean and dirty mice over time.

claim: Memory T cells exhibit considerable heterogeneity in their function, circulation patterns, response to re-challenge, and capacities for proliferative self-renewal and survival.
source: In mice, memory T cells exhibit considerable heterogeneity in their function, circulation patterns, response to re-challenge, and capacities for proliferative self-renewal and survival (Farber, 2000; Kaech and Wherry, 2007; Jameson and Masopust, 2009; Gossel et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to established literature.

claim: In uninfected naive mice, there are at least two distinct populations of recirculating cells distinguished by their expression of CD62L: CD44hi CD62L− effector memory (TEM) and CD44hi CD62L+ central memory (TCM) cells.
source: In uninfected naive mice, there are at least two distinct populations of recirculating cells distinguished by their expression of the lymph node homing receptor L-selectin (CD62L); CD44hi CD62L− effector memory (TEM) and CD44hi CD62L+ central memory (TCM) cells.
evidence: This is a description of established phenotypic markers used to identify memory T cell subsets.

claim: Memory-phenotype cells are capable of making rapid cross-reactive responses during primary infections.
source: There is also evidence that MP cells are capable of making rapid cross-reactive responses during primary infections (Min and Paul, 2005).
evidence: This capability is supported by citation to Min and Paul, 2005.

claim: Memory-phenotype cells represent the majority of the memory compartment in specific pathogen-free (SPF) mice.
source: Given that MP cells represent the majority of the memory compartment in specific pathogen-free (SPF) mice (Kawabe et al., 2017)
evidence: This quantitative observation is supported by citation to Kawabe et al., 2017.

claim: Cd28−/− mice have greatly reduced numbers of memory-phenotype cells.
source: Cd28−/− mice have greatly reduced numbers of MP cells (Kotani et al., 2006)
evidence: This observation in knockout mice is supported by citation to Kotani et al., 2006.

claim: Memory-phenotype cells are generated not only in lymphopenia but also constitutively under replete conditions throughout life.
source: and indeed MP cells are generated not only in lymphopenia but also constitutively under replete conditions throughout life (Gossel et al., 2017; Kawabe et al., 2017).
evidence: This observation is supported by citations to two studies.

claim: There is a positive correlation between the affinity of naive CD4+ T cells to self-antigens and the potential for differentiating into memory-phenotype cells.
source: There is a positive correlation between the affinity of naive CD4+ T cells to self-antigens and the potential for differentiating into MP cells (Kawabe et al., 2017)
evidence: This correlation is supported by citation to Kawabe et al., 2017.

claim: Self-reactivity is positively correlated to reactivity to foreign antigens.
source: although self-reactivity is also positively correlated to reactivity to foreign antigens (Mandl et al., 2013).
evidence: This correlation is supported by citation to Mandl et al., 2013.

claim: Broad-spectrum antibiotics fail to prevent conversion of naive T cells to memory-phenotype cells following adoptive transfer in vivo.
source: Stronger evidence supporting an autoreactive stimulus comes from the failure of broad-spectrum antibiotics to prevent conversion of naive T cells to MP cells following adoptive transfer in vivo
evidence: This experimental observation supports the role of self-antigens.

claim: Mice raised in germ-free conditions contain similar numbers of memory-phenotype cells as those in SPF conditions.
source: and the observation that mice raised in germ-free conditions contain similar numbers of MP cells as those in SPF conditions (Kawabe et al., 2017).
evidence: This observation is supported by citation to Kawabe et al., 2017.

claim: Mice raised in more antigenically diverse environments exhibit larger peripheral memory CD8+ T cell pools than SPF mice.
source: However, there is also a role for foreign environmental antigen in generating T cell memory compartments, since mice raised in more antigenically diverse environments, but still in the absence of overt infection, exhibit larger peripheral memory CD8+ T cell pools than SPF mice (Beura et al., 2016).
evidence: This observation is supported by citation to Beura et al., 2016.

claim: There is evidence that some memory-phenotype CD8+ subpopulations are generated in the thymus.
source: Amongst CD8+ lineage cells, there is evidence that some MP subpopulations are generated in the thymus (Lee et al., 2011).
evidence: This observation is supported by citation to Lee et al., 2011.

claim: It has been suggested that memory-phenotype CD4+ cells derive from peripheral naive phenotype cells in a thymus-independent fashion.
source: In the case of CD4+ lineage cells, it has been suggested that MP cells derive from peripheral naive phenotype cells in a thymus-independent fashion (Kawabe et al., 2017).
evidence: This suggestion is supported by citation to Kawabe et al., 2017.

claim: Both CD4+ TCM and TEM are produced constitutively in adult mice.
source: While both CD4+ TCM and TEM are produced constitutively in adult mice (Gossel et al., 2017)
evidence: This observation is supported by citation to Gossel et al., 2017.

claim: Total numbers of CD4+ naive T cells and TCM and TEM cells in busulfan chimeric mice were normal, in comparison to untreated wild-type controls.
source: Total numbers of CD4+ naive T cells and TCM and TEM cells in these busulfan chimeric mice were normal, in comparison to untreated wild-type (WT) controls (Figure 1—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This observation validates the busulfan treatment model and is supported by data shown in a figure.

claim: The busulfan treatment regime left peripheral compartments intact.
source: confirming that the busulfan treatment regime left peripheral compartments intact (Hogan et al., 2015; Gossel et al., 2017).
evidence: This conclusion is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: From age 10 weeks onwards, the numbers of CD4+ naive T cells in mice from clean and dirty environments were broadly similar.
source: From age 10 weeks onwards, the numbers of CD4+ naive T cells in mice from clean and dirty environments were broadly similar (Figure 1B, left panel).
evidence: This observation is supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The total sizes of all circulating memory CD4+ T cell subsets remained relatively stable over the time frame of analysis.
source: The total sizes (host+donor) of all circulating memory CD4+ T cell subsets remained relatively stable over the time frame of analysis
evidence: This observation is based on the longitudinal data collected in the study.

claim: Memory CD4+ T cell subsets were significantly larger in dirty mice at age 10 weeks.
source: but were significantly larger in dirty mice (Figure 1B, right panels) at age 10 weeks.
evidence: This observation is supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Following BMT, donor-derived memory T cells accumulated in similar numbers in the two environments.
source: Following BMT, donor-derived memory T cells accumulated in similar numbers in the two environments (Figure 1C).
evidence: This observation is supported by data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: There is a lower proportional replacement of pre-existing memory cells with donor memory cells in dirty mice.
source: Therefore, these two observations result in a lower proportional replacement of pre-existing memory cells with donor memory cells in dirty mice (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The kinetic of donor chimerism in CD4+ TEM clearly lagged that of CD4+ TCM.
source: The kinetic of donor chimerism in CD4+ TEM clearly lagged that of CD4+ TCM (Figure 1D)
evidence: This observation is supported by data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: TEM is ruled out as a direct predictor of TCM accumulation.
source: ruling out TEM as a direct predictor of TCM accumulation.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the observation that TEM chimerism lags TCM chimerism.

claim: There is clearly stronger support for TCM cells rather than naive T cells as a predictor of TEM production.
source: We found clearly stronger support for TCM cells rather than naive T cells as a predictor of TEM production (Table 1).
evidence: This conclusion is based on model comparison using AICc values shown in Table 1.

claim: There is almost no support for the homogeneous or resistant memory models.
source: We found almost no support for the homogeneous or resistant memory models.
evidence: This conclusion is based on model comparison using statistical criteria.

claim: For TCM the age-dependent loss model was strongly favoured statistically.
source: For TCM the age-dependent loss was strongly favoured statistically
evidence: This conclusion is based on model comparison using statistical criteria.

claim: For TEM the two-phase model had the strongest support.
source: while for TEM the two-phase model had the strongest support (fits shown in Figure 3).
evidence: This conclusion is based on model comparison and fits shown in Figure 3.

claim: There is a progressive lengthening of clonal lifetimes in both memory subsets and environments.
source: A robust conclusion, however, is that we find a progressive lengthening of clonal lifetimes in both memory subsets and environments, with newly recruited memory being lost on timescales of days to weeks, and more established memory persisting for several months (Figure 4).
evidence: This conclusion is supported by parameter estimates shown in Figure 4.

claim: Newly recruited memory is lost on timescales of days to weeks.
source: with newly recruited memory being lost on timescales of days to weeks
evidence: This quantitative estimate is derived from model fitting to the data.

claim: More established memory persists for several months.
source: and more established memory persisting for several months (Figure 4).
evidence: This quantitative estimate is derived from model fitting and shown in Figure 4.

claim: There are no substantial differences in rates of loss of memory cells between clean and dirty mice.
source: and no substantial differences in their rates of loss (Figure 4 and Table 2).
evidence: This conclusion is based on parameter estimates shown in Figure 4 and Table 2.

claim: Antigenic stimuli common to both environments drive the continuous generation of new CD4+ effector and central memory T cells in adult mice.
source: Therefore, we infer that antigenic stimuli common to both environments drive the continuous generation of new CD4+ effector and central memory T cells in adult mice, at total rates that are proportional to the sizes of their precursor populations.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the similarity of recruitment rates in clean and dirty mice.

claim: The rate of generation of new memory in both environments wanes with age.
source: suggesting that the rate of generation of new memory in both environments wanes with age, and/or that more established memory has a competitive advantage over recently recruited cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that donor chimerism in TCM is lower than in naive T cells.

claim: More established memory has a competitive advantage over recently recruited cells.
source: suggesting that the rate of generation of new memory in both environments wanes with age, and/or that more established memory has a competitive advantage over recently recruited cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that donor chimerism in TCM is lower than in naive T cells.

claim: CD4+ naive T cell numbers decay exponentially in both clean and dirty adult mice due to thymic involution.
source: due to thymic involution, CD4+ naive T cell numbers decay exponentially in both clean and dirty adult mice (Figure 1B) with population half lives of 228 days (95% CI 227–231 days) and 143 (142-144) days, respectively.
evidence: This observation is based on fitting exponential decay curves to the data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The population half-life of CD4+ naive T cells in clean mice is 228 days (95% CI 227–231 days).
source: with population half lives of 228 days (95% CI 227–231 days)
evidence: This quantitative estimate is derived from fitting to the data.

claim: The population half-life of CD4+ naive T cells in dirty mice is 143 days (95% CI 142-144 days).
source: and 143 (142-144) days, respectively.
evidence: This quantitative estimate is derived from fitting to the data.

claim: The limited replacement of host CD4+ TCM by donor cells derives from the decline in naive T cell numbers with age, slow average rates of turnover, and the increased persistence of more established memory cells.
source: Therefore, the limited replacement of host CD4+ TCM by donor cells derives from the decline in naive T cell numbers with age, slow average rates of turnover, and the increased persistence of more established memory cells.
evidence: This is a synthesis of multiple observations and model predictions.

claim: The two-phase model predicts that the establishment of memory is relatively inefficient, with 'fast' populations lost over timescales of days and only a small proportion surviving to become more persistent 'slow' memory.
source: The two-phase model predicts that the establishment of memory is relatively inefficient, with 'fast' populations lost over timescales of days and only a small proportion of these surviving to become more persistent 'slow' memory (∼2–10% of TEM, and ∼3–5% of TCM; Table 2).
evidence: This is a prediction from the two-phase model with parameter estimates shown in Table 2.

claim: Approximately 2–10% of TEM in the fast phase survive to become slow memory.
source: (∼2–10% of TEM, and ∼3–5% of TCM; Table 2).
evidence: This quantitative estimate is derived from the two-phase model parameters shown in Table 2.

claim: Approximately 3–5% of TCM in the fast phase survive to become slow memory.
source: (∼2–10% of TEM, and ∼3–5% of TCM; Table 2).
evidence: This quantitative estimate is derived from the two-phase model parameters shown in Table 2.

claim: The substantial constitutive influxes maintain the fast and slow populations at comparable sizes.
source: Despite this inefficiency, the substantial constitutive influxes maintain the fast and slow populations at comparable sizes, consistent with our previous analysis of BrdU labelling of CD4+ TCM and TEM in WT mice (Gossel et al., 2017).
evidence: This conclusion is consistent with previous experimental observations using BrdU labelling.

claim: The age-dependent loss model makes lower estimates of the force of recruitment into memory than the two-phase model.
source: In contrast, the age-dependent loss model makes lower estimates of the force of recruitment into memory (Figure 4, left panels)
evidence: This comparison is based on parameter estimates shown in Figure 4.

claim: The age-dependent loss model predicts more efficient establishment of memory, with newly generated memory having clonal half-lives of 20–40 days.
source: but predicts more efficient establishment, with newly generated memory having clonal half-lives of 20–40 days and a much greater proportion persisting longer term (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a prediction from the age-dependent loss model shown in the supplementary figure.

claim: The larger, relatively stable TCM and TEM populations in dirty mice must derive from their establishment in greater numbers in the first few weeks of life.
source: Given the similarity of the rates of generation of memory in clean and dirty adult mice, and of their rates of turnover, we infer that the larger, relatively stable TCM and TEM populations in dirty mice (Figure 3A) must derive from their establishment in greater numbers in the first few weeks of life.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the similarity of adult parameters but different population sizes.

claim: The differences in compartment sizes in the two environments are sustained well into adulthood by the very slow loss of these early memory populations.
source: The differences in compartment sizes in the two environments are then sustained well into adulthood by the very slow loss of these early memory populations.
evidence: This is an inference based on the slow turnover rates estimated for established memory.

claim: The model slightly underestimated TCM numbers in clean adult mice and failed to capture their rapid accumulation up to age 4 weeks.
source: The model slightly underestimated TCM numbers in clean adult mice and failed to capture their rapid accumulation up to age 4 weeks.
evidence: This is an observation about the model's predictive performance when applied to young mice.

claim: Using the observed timecourse of TCM in clean WT mice as a source, the establishment of the TEM compartment was predicted remarkably well by the adult parameters from the favoured two-phase model.
source: In contrast, using the observed timecourse of TCM in clean WT mice as a source (Figure 5A, right panel), the establishment of the TEM compartment was predicted remarkably well by the adult parameters from the favoured two-phase model (Figure 5B, right panel).
evidence: This observation demonstrates the predictive power of the model for TEM development.

claim: Using adult dirty mouse parameters underestimated TCM numbers at age 14 weeks by a factor of approximately 4.
source: This prediction underestimated TCM numbers at age 14 weeks by a factor of approximately 4 (Figure 5C, left panel).
evidence: This observation indicates that the force of recruitment must be higher in young dirty mice.

claim: Mice in the clean facility experience a slightly elevated force of recruitment into TCM early in life.
source: We conclude that to account for memory T cell numbers in adulthood, mice in the clean facility experience a slightly elevated force of recruitment into TCM early in life
evidence: This conclusion is based on comparing model predictions with observed data.

claim: The force of recruitment into TCM is much larger in dirtier mice early in life, presumably deriving from greater levels of exposure to environmental antigens.
source: and this force is much larger in dirtier mice, presumably deriving from greater levels of exposure to environmental antigens.
evidence: This conclusion is based on comparing model predictions with observed data and is attributed to environmental differences.

claim: Substantial numbers of both TCM and TEM memory-phenotype cells were recovered from germ-free mice aged between 40 and 200d.
source: Consistent with these earlier studies, substantial numbers of both TCM and TEM MP cells were recovered from GF mice aged between 40 and 200d
evidence: This observation is based on experimental data from germ-free mice.

claim: The generation of memory-phenotype cells does not depend exclusively on commensal-derived foreign antigens.
source: confirming that the generation of MP cells does not depend exclusively on commensal-derived foreign antigens (Figure 6A).
evidence: This conclusion is based on the presence of MP cells in germ-free mice shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The memory CD4+ T cell compartments of germ-free mice were significantly smaller than in the SPF mice in all facilities.
source: However, the memory CD4+ T cell compartments of GF mice, enumerated from spleen and lymph nodes combined, were significantly smaller than in the SPF mice in all facilities.
evidence: This observation is based on comparing cell counts across different housing conditions.

claim: Clean mice from KI and UCL had similar-sized memory compartments.
source: Clean mice from KI and UCL had similar-sized memory compartments
evidence: This observation is based on comparing cell counts from two clean facilities.

claim: Both clean facilities had substantially smaller memory compartments than those in mice from the dirty facility (NIMR).
source: and in turn both were substantially smaller than those in mice from the dirty facility (NIMR) (Figure 6A).
evidence: This observation is based on comparing cell counts shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The dirty mice played host to around five times the number of memory-phenotype cells found in germ-free mice.
source: Indeed, the dirty mice played host to around five times the number of MP cells found in GF mice
evidence: This quantitative comparison is based on cell count data.

claim: Antigens from commensal organisms are a substantial driver of memory-phenotype cell expansion.
source: indicating that antigens from commensal organisms are a substantial driver of MP cell expansion.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the difference in MP cell numbers between GF and dirty mice.

claim: A substantial fraction of memory-phenotype cells in germ-free mice expressed Ki67.
source: A substantial fraction of MP cells in GF mice expressed Ki67 (Figure 6B)
evidence: This observation is based on flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Ki67 expression indicates cell cycle activity within the previous 3–4 days.
source: indicating cell cycle activity within the previous 3–4 days (Gossel et al., 2017).
evidence: This interpretation of Ki67 expression is supported by citation to Gossel et al., 2017.

claim: The proportion of Ki67+ memory-phenotype cells was broadly similar across germ-free, clean, and dirty environments.
source: This proportion was broadly similar to that in mice from both clean and dirty environments
evidence: This observation is based on comparing Ki67 expression data across environments.

claim: The level of proliferation of CD4+ memory-phenotype T cells in adult mice was relatively insensitive to environmentally derived stimuli.
source: indicating that the level of proliferation of CD4+ MP T cells in adult mice was relatively insensitive to environmentally derived stimuli.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the similarity of Ki67 expression across environments.

claim: Germ-free mice needed approximately 0.4 times the force of recruitment in clean adult mice to seed CD4+ TCM at observed levels.
source: GF mice needed approximately 0.4 times the force of recruitment in clean adult mice
evidence: This quantitative estimate is derived from model fitting to achieve observed TCM numbers.

claim: Younger clean mice needed a force of recruitment approximately 1.1 times greater than clean adult mice.
source: younger clean mice needed a force approximately 1.1 times greater
evidence: This quantitative estimate is derived from model fitting to achieve observed TCM numbers.

claim: Dirty mice required a 2.7-fold increase in force of recruitment compared to clean adult mice.
source: and dirty mice required a 2.7-fold increase.
evidence: This quantitative estimate is derived from model fitting to achieve observed TCM numbers.

claim: After accounting for the different TCM population sizes, the force of recruitment from TCM to TEM estimated in clean adult mice was sufficient to account for TEM numbers in all three environments.
source: Remarkably, after accounting for the different TCM population sizes, the force of recruitment from TCM to TEM estimated in clean adult mice was also sufficient to account for TEM numbers in all three environments (Figure 7, right panel).
evidence: This conclusion is based on model predictions shown in Figure 7.

claim: Approximately 2- to 3-fold increases or decreases in the force of recruitment into CD4+ TCM observed in clean adult mice were sufficient to explain their numbers in dirty mice or germ-free mice.
source: In summary, this analysis showed that approximately 2- to 3-fold increases or decreases in the force of recruitment into CD4+ TCM observed in clean adult (UCL) mice were sufficient to explain their numbers in dirty mice from NIMR or GF mice.
evidence: This is a summary of the quantitative modeling results.

claim: The rate of development of TEM from TCM appeared to be independent of both mouse age and environment.
source: However the subsequent rate of development of TEM from TCM appeared to be independent of both mouse age and environment
evidence: This conclusion is based on the ability of a single parameter set to predict TEM in all environments.

claim: Differences in the numbers of TEM could be explained simply by the differences in the size of the TCM precursor population.
source: and differences in the numbers of TEM could be explained simply by the differences in the size of the TCM precursor population.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the modeling results showing TEM numbers depend on TCM numbers.

claim: The rate of generation of CD4+ TCM from naive T cells in young mice reflects both self antigens and the level of exposure to environmental antigens.
source: These results suggest that the rate of generation of CD4+ TCM from naive T cells in young mice reflects both self antigens and the level of exposure to environmental antigens
evidence: This conclusion is based on comparing GF, clean, and dirty mice.

claim: The rate of differentiation from TCM to TEM is largely insensitive to self antigens and environmental antigens.
source: but that the rate of differentiation from TCM to TEM is largely insensitive to these forces.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the constant rate of TCM to TEM conversion across environments.

claim: Self recognition contributes to tonic recruitment into the TCM and TEM pools in adults, the kinetic substructure and maintenance of these compartments throughout life, and their generation/establishment early in life.
source: Our analyses indicate that self recognition contributes to all these processes
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the study's analyses.

claim: The contribution of reactivity to commensal antigens is largely restricted to the neonatal period.
source: but that the contribution of reactivity to commensal antigens is largely restricted to the neonatal period.
evidence: This is a key conclusion from comparing adult and neonatal dynamics across environments.

claim: Memory CD4+ T cell division, as reported by Ki67, was substantial and largely independent of the level of commensals.
source: We also found that memory CD4+ T cell division, as reported by Ki67, was substantial and largely independent of the level of commensals.
evidence: This observation is based on Ki67 expression data across environments.

claim: The common levels of Ki67 across environments, together with findings that rates of memory generation and net loss were insensitive to environment, support the conclusion that self-recognition is the major driver of both recruitment and proliferative renewal in adult memory compartments.
source: However, the common levels of Ki67 across environments, together with our findings from the adult clean and dirty chimeric mice that the rates of memory generation and net loss were insensitive to environment, support our conclusion that self-recognition is the major driver of both recruitment and proliferative renewal in adult memory compartments.
evidence: This conclusion synthesizes multiple lines of evidence from the study.

claim: CD4+ TCM and TEM numbers in mice raised in dirty environments were 3–5 times greater than those in either germ-free or cleaner IVC or SPF facilities.
source: Commensals did, however, have a substantial impact upon the sizes of the memory compartments generated early in life. CD4+ TCM and TEM numbers in mice raised in dirty environments were 3–5 times greater than those in either GF or cleaner IVC or SPF facilities
evidence: This quantitative comparison is based on cell count data.

claim: These differences in memory cell numbers could be explained by differences in the forces of recruitment of CD4+ TCM during ontogeny.
source: and these differences could be explained by differences in the forces of recruitment of CD4+ TCM during ontogeny.
evidence: This conclusion is based on modeling results.

claim: The estimated seven-fold difference in force of recruitment between germ-free and dirty mice suggests that self-recognition only accounts for approximately 14% of the memory compartment in dirty mice.
source: The estimated seven-fold difference in this force between GF and dirty mice prompts the simple interpretation that self-recognition only accounts for ∼14% of the memory compartment in dirty mice.
evidence: This interpretation is based on the ratio of forces of recruitment in GF vs dirty mice.

claim: It is possible that smaller memory compartment sizes in germ-free mice also derive from their smaller lymph nodes.
source: but it is possible that their smaller sizes in GF mice also derive from their smaller lymph nodes.
evidence: This is a speculation about an alternative explanation for the observations.

claim: Bacterial stimulation of DCs is required for their migration into lymph nodes.
source: Bacterial stimulation of DCs is required for their migration into lymph nodes, and these DCs are required for their normal development (Wendland et al., 2011; Moussion and Girard, 2011; Zhang et al., 2016).
evidence: This mechanistic relationship is supported by citations to three studies.

claim: It is not straightforward to separate the indirect influence of commensals on lymphoid development from any direct influences upon memory generation.
source: Therefore, it is not straightforward to separate the indirect influence of commensals on lymphoid development from any direct influences upon memory generation.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of the complexity in interpreting the GF mouse data.

claim: It is possible that some of the additional force of recruitment in neonates derives not from commensals but from lymphopenia.
source: It is also possible that some of the additional force of recruitment in neonates derives not from commensals but from lymphopenia, which can drive naive T cells to acquire a memory phenotype (Min et al., 2003).
evidence: This is a speculation about an alternative mechanism, supported by citation.

claim: Lymphopenia can drive naive T cells to acquire a memory phenotype.
source: which can drive naive T cells to acquire a memory phenotype (Min et al., 2003).
evidence: This mechanism is supported by citation to Min et al., 2003.

claim: Environment impacted not only memory but also naive T cells.
source: We observed that environment not only impacted memory but also naive T cells.
evidence: This observation is based on comparing naive T cell dynamics in clean and dirty mice.

claim: Naive T cell numbers naturally decline with age, but this decline was almost twice as fast in dirty mice than in genetically identical mice housed in cleaner facilities.
source: Their numbers naturally decline with age, but this decline was almost twice as fast in dirty mice than in genetically identical mice housed in cleaner facilities (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A; numbers halve every 228d (95% CI 227–231) in clean mice, and 143d (142-144) in dirty mice).
evidence: This observation is based on fitting decay curves to naive T cell data shown in the supplementary figure.

claim: The difference in naive T cell decline likely derives from a more rapid reduction in thymic output with age in the dirty environment.
source: This difference likely derives from a more rapid reduction in thymic output with age in the dirty environment, and not differences in lifespans of CD4+ naive T cells in the two environments
evidence: This interpretation is based on comparing thymic and peripheral naive T cell dynamics.

claim: Single positive thymocytes at the latest stage of thymic development decline with half-lives of 282d (281-308) in clean mice and 151d (150-159) in dirty mice.
source: because we see similar rates of decline in the numbers of single positive thymocytes at the latest stage of thymic development (halving every every 282d (281-308) in clean mice, 151d (150-159) in dirty mice; data not shown).
evidence: This observation is based on analysis of thymic cell data.

claim: Another consequence of life in a more antigenically diverse environment is more rapid involution of the thymus.
source: Therefore, it appears that another consequence of life in a more antigenically diverse environment is more rapid involution of the thymus.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the faster decline in thymic output in dirty mice.

claim: It is possible that the effect of environment on thymic involution derives from the stress or inflammation associated with an increased commensal burden.
source: It is possible that this effect derives from the stress or inflammation associated with an increased commensal burden, or is somehow a consequence of expanded memory populations
evidence: This is speculation about potential mechanisms underlying the observed effect.

claim: Environmental factors can impact the maintenance of naive T cells.
source: but whatever the mechanism, our data clearly indicate that environmental factors can impact the maintenance of naive T cells.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the observed differences in naive T cell dynamics between environments.

claim: Memory cell numbers only vary by a factor of 2–3 between clean and dirty mice.
source: Since memory cell numbers only vary by a factor of 2–3 between clean and dirty mice
evidence: This quantitative observation is based on cell count data.

claim: Estimates of loss rates were similar in the two environments.
source: and indeed our estimates of loss rates were similar in the two environments.
evidence: This observation is based on parameter estimates from model fitting.

claim: There is arguably little evidence for homeostatic regulation of circulating memory T cells in SPF mice.
source: While we cannot rule it out at higher cell densities, there is arguably little evidence for homeostatic regulation of circulating memory T cells in SPF mice.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the observations in the study.

claim: A range of relatively stable memory compartment sizes were observed in the different containment facilities.
source: We observed a range of relatively stable memory compartment sizes in the different containment facilities
evidence: This observation is based on cell count data across facilities.

claim: Memory compartments do not appear to fill up rapidly with large clones in very young mice.
source: these memory compartments do not appear to fill up rapidly with large clones in very young mice, which might occur if division or loss rates are sensitive to total pool size
evidence: This observation argues against strong homeostatic regulation.

claim: Memory compartments appear to be expandable following multiple infections in older animals.
source: and they appear to be expandable following multiple infections in older animals (Vezys et al., 2009).
evidence: This observation is supported by citation to Vezys et al., 2009.

claim: The models yielded robust conclusions regarding the nature and magnitudes of the forces generating CD4+ TCM and TEM.
source: The models yielded robust conclusions regarding the nature and magnitudes of the forces generating CD4+ TCM and TEM
evidence: This is a summary statement about the modeling results.

claim: The models confirmed the existence of heterogeneity within both TCM and TEM subsets.
source: and the existence of heterogeneity within both subsets, consistent with previous reports by ourselves and others of subpopulations of CD4+ MP cells with distinct rates of division and turnover (Younes et al., 2011; Gossel et al., 2017).
evidence: This conclusion is consistent with previous studies cited.

claim: Resolving the details of kinetic substructure in lymphocyte populations is challenging.
source: However, these models are abstractions, and resolving the details of kinetic substructure in lymphocyte populations is challenging (Ganusov et al., 2010).
evidence: This acknowledgment of methodological challenges is supported by citation.

claim: For CD4+ TCM in adult mice there is evidence for slow and continuous changes in their net loss rates as cells age.
source: For CD4+ TCM in adult mice we found evidence for slow and continuous changes in their net loss rates as cells age
evidence: This conclusion is based on model comparison favoring the age-dependent loss model.

claim: Additional support for continuous changes in net loss rates comes from the slow rate at which Ki67 levels in donor and host memory cells converge in adult busulfan chimeras.
source: and additional support for such a process comes from the slow rate at which Ki67 levels in donor and host memory cells converge in adult busulfan chimeras.
evidence: This observation provides independent support for the age-dependent loss model.

claim: The data for TEM in adult mice more strongly supported a discrete two-phase model with a relatively rapid transition from fast to slow memory.
source: In contrast, the data for TEM in adult mice, and the predictions of their accumulation in younger mice, more strongly supported a discrete two-phase model with a relatively rapid transition from fast to slow memory.
evidence: This conclusion is based on model comparison and predictive performance.

claim: A previous study used short-term BrdU labelling to identify populations in both TCM and TEM subsets that divide and die rapidly.
source: Our previous study of CD4+ TCM and TEM homeostasis in adult mice used short-term BrdU labelling to identify populations in both subsets that divide and die rapidly (Gossel et al., 2017)
evidence: This refers to findings from a previous study by the authors.

claim: It seems likely that both memory-phenotype cell subsets are more heterogeneous than any one of the models suggests.
source: Overall, although, it seems likely that both MP cell subsets are more heterogeneous than any one of our models suggests.
evidence: This is an interpretation acknowledging the limitations of the models.

claim: One possibility is that memory-phenotype T cells are generated with a distribution of net loss rates, and those clones with greater intrinsic fitness are selected for over time.
source: One possibility is that MP T cells are generated with a distribution of net loss rates, and those clones with greater intrinsic fitness (lower net loss rates) are simply selected for over time.
evidence: This is a speculation about an alternative mechanism of heterogeneity.

claim: Such a selection mechanism could explain the under-representation of donor cells in the memory compartments of busulfan chimeric mice.
source: Such a mechanism – a generalisation of the simple 'resistant memory' model we rejected here – could explain the under-representation of donor cells in the memory compartments of busulfan chimeric mice
evidence: This is speculation about how an alternative mechanism could explain the observations.

claim: The selection mechanism may be difficult to distinguish from the model of gradual changes in fitness with cell age.
source: and may be difficult to distinguish from our model of gradual changes in fitness with cell age; indeed the two mechanisms are not mutually exclusive.
evidence: This acknowledges the difficulty in distinguishing between alternative mechanisms.

claim: Division of memory-phenotype cells is dependent on TCR.
source: Division of MP cells is dependent on TCR (Seddon et al., 2003)
evidence: This mechanistic requirement is supported by citation to Seddon et al., 2003.

claim: Division of memory-phenotype cells is dependent on CD28 costimulation signaling.
